items.title: Cisco Secure Firewall Adaptive Security Appliance and Secure Firewall Threat Defense Software Remote Access SSL VPN Tunnel Denial of Service Vulnerability
items.one_liner: Critical Cisco ASA and FTD SSL VPN software contains an unauthenticated remote DoS vulnerability that requires an immediate vendor patch.
items.summary: A high-severity denial-of-service vulnerability has been identified in the Remote Access SSL VPN service of Cisco Secure Firewall ASA and FTD software, tracked as CVE-2026-76418 with a security impact rating of high. The issue arises from logic errors when secondary authentication is configured on a tunnel group, which allows an unauthenticated, remote attacker to trigger an unexpected device reload via a crafted request. This unexpected reload drops active connections and results in a persistent denial-of-service condition for users relying on the gateway. Cisco has released software updates to address the issue, but notes that no workarounds are available to mitigate the vulnerability without patching.
items.bottom_line: Unauthenticated attackers can crash Cisco Secure Firewall ASA and FTD devices via crafted SSL VPN connection requests when secondary authentication is configured.

claims.text: A vulnerability in the Remote Access SSL VPN service of Cisco Secure Firewall Adaptive Security Appliance (ASA) Software and Cisco Secure Firewall Threat Defense (FTD) Software could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause the device to reload unexpectedly, resulting in a denial of service (DoS) condition.

items.title: CVE-2026-111497: Google Google Brotli Unchecked Return Value Vulnerability
items.one_liner: CISA adds Google Brotli memory corruption vulnerability CVE-2026-111497 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
items.summary: CISA has added CVE-2026-111497, an unchecked return value vulnerability in Google Brotli, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. The flaw allows remote unauthenticated attackers to corrupt adjacent decoder state memory, disclose sensitive memory information, trigger a denial of service, or potentially achieve arbitrary code execution via a crafted compressed stream. Federal agencies are mandated to apply vendor mitigations by November 10, 2026, in compliance with Binding Operational Directive 26-04.
items.bottom_line: Organizations must patch Google Brotli to prevent memory corruption and potential remote code execution via crafted compressed streams.

items.one_liner: GitLab versions 19.4.2, 19.3.5, and 19.2.8 patch critical vulnerabilities including CI/CD integer overflows and Duo Agent flaws.
items.summary: GitLab has issued critical security patch releases for versions 19.4.2, 19.3.5, and 19.2.8 across Community and Enterprise editions to address multiple high-severity vulnerabilities. Notable flaws patched include an integer overflow in the CI/CD regular expression compiler, cross-site scripting in syntax highlighting, improper authorizations in downstream pipelines, and an input neutralization issue in the GitLab Duo Agent Platform. Self-managed instances are strongly urged to upgrade immediately as GitLab.com and Dedicated tenants have already been patched.

items.title: Researchers uncover Volt Typhoon’s covert, ephemeral network
items.one_liner: Volt Typhoon uses rapidly rotating 'Silent Train' SOHO router networks to burrow into critical infrastructure undetected.
items.summary: The Chinese state-backed hacking group Volt Typhoon has utilized a covert, ephemeral network infrastructure dubbed 'Silent Train' since late 2023 to infiltrate US critical infrastructure undetected. According to a report by Lumen Technologies' Black Lotus Labs, the threat group rapidly rotates through a chain of compromised SOHO routers, IoT devices, and enterprise gear—assembling and dismantling individual infrastructure chains in under two minutes. This ephemeral framework allows them to exploit edge device zero-days and maintain persistent access across sectors including telecom, government, defense, and energy. The group intensified its use of Silent Train following the FBI's early 2024 disruption of the KV Botnet, abusing devices from over 27 manufacturers such as Fortinet, Cisco, and Ivanti.
key_facts: Average session duration: Roughly four hours
items.bottom_line: Volt Typhoon maintains persistent access to critical infrastructure by rapidly assembling and dismantling ephemeral chains of compromised edge devices.

claims.text: Volt Typhoon, a China-government backed hacking group that has infiltrated America’s critical infrastructure networks for years, has consistently built and dismantled ephemeral malicious infrastructure to burrow into hundreds of sensitive systems undetected, Lumen Technologies’ Black Lotus Labs said in a Wednesday report.

items.title: Japan's GMO Offers $1 Million Bounty to Catch Hackers Behind FX Trading Cloud Breach
items.one_liner: GMO Internet offers a $1 million bounty after attackers breach its FX trading cloud service and demand $50 million.
items.summary: Japan's GMO Internet Group has launched a $1 million cybercrime bounty program to capture the hackers who breached its Onamae.com Desktop Cloud service after refusing a $50 million extortion demand. The attackers compromised 26,739 servers used for FX trading, exfiltrated customer information, and posted stolen data online before their infrastructure domains were seized. The breach exposed credentials stored within trading applications like MetaTrader, leading to unauthorized trading activity reported by customers and brokers like OANDA Japan. The bounty program offers rewards for tips leading to arrests or international wanted notices.
items.bottom_line: GMO Internet Group is offering a $1 million bounty for tips leading to the arrest of hackers who breached its cloud service and compromised FX trading credentials.

items.title: Hackers Infect 953 Online Stores With Scanner-Evading JavaScript, Mostly on Magento
items.one_liner: A persistent e-commerce malware campaign has compromised nearly a thousand Magento stores using bot-filtering JavaScript loaders.
items.summary: An ongoing campaign active since July 2025 has infected 953 online stores, predominantly running Magento, with scanner-evading malicious JavaScript loaders. Dutch security firm Sansec discovered that attackers inject malicious stubs into Magento's `cms_block` database table, utilizing five distinct domains including `deepveindrilling[.]com` to serve payloads. The injected scripts perform browser fingerprinting and environment checks to filter out security scanners and bots, ensuring payloads are delivered exclusively to real shoppers. Initial access to at least 471 stores was achieved by exploiting vulnerabilities such as PolyShell (CVE-2026-48356) and SessionReaper (CVE-2025-54236).
items.bottom_line: Attackers are actively exploiting unpatched Magento vulnerabilities like PolyShell to inject persistent, scanner-evading JavaScript loaders into online stores.

items.title: Gheist Uses Stolen GitHub Tokens to Steal Private Repository Secrets via Actions Logs
items.one_liner: The 'Gheist' campaign uses stolen GitHub tokens to harvest private repository secrets via Actions logs.
items.summary: An automated threat campaign tracked as 'Gheist' is actively exploiting stolen GitHub tokens to plant malicious workflows that expose repository secrets into GitHub Actions logs. The attackers create unauthorized branches named 'ci-sync-' and commit workflow configurations designed to dump base32-encoded environment secrets before downloading the logs via the API and deleting the runs. Cloud security firm Wiz discovered that the campaign has compromised over 850 accounts and recovered more than 13,500 planted branches across personal and enterprise private repositories. Because GitHub's secret masking fails to protect base32-encoded strings, organizations must rotate exposed secrets and revoke compromised tokens immediately.
items.bottom_line: Compromised GitHub tokens allow attackers to automatically extract and exfiltrate private repository secrets through Actions log downloads.

items.title: Hacker stole personnel data about thousands of Homeland Security employees, including CBP and ICE agents
items.one_liner: A data breach at the Department of Homeland Security's Okta SSO exposed personnel records for over 40,000 employees, including ICE and CISA staff.
items.summary: Personally identifiable information belonging to more than 40,000 U.S. Department of Homeland Security employees was published online after a breach earlier this year. A hacker operating under the handle 'Department of Peace' exfiltrated the data from an Okta single sign-on system, exposing names, job titles, office locations, and contact details. The affected personnel include over 21,000 U.S. Customs and Border Protection staff, 10,000 Immigration and Customs Enforcement personnel, and nearly 1,000 CISA cybersecurity staff. The stolen records were shared via DDoSecrets after being provided to journalist maia arson crimew.
items.bottom_line: A hacker leaked personnel records for over 40,000 DHS employees, including border agents and cybersecurity staffers, stolen from an Okta single sign-on system.

items.title: php2shell in Practice: Exploitable, Conditional, and Hard to Mass-Exploit
items.one_liner: Exploiting php2shell is significantly harder than public PoCs suggest due to strict heap layout requirements and version-specific binary offsets.
items.summary: The 'php2shell' vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) are critical pre-auth RCE flaws in the PHP core that are exploitable but highly conditional. Successful exploitation requires specific heap layouts, version-dependent offsets, and often relies on non-default PHP configurations like 'display_errors=On'. While public exploits exist, they are often unreliable or require significant effort to tailor to specific server builds and architectures.
items.bottom_line: Do not assume public php2shell exploits will work out-of-the-box; successful exploitation requires deep knowledge of the target's specific PHP build and memory layout.

claims.text: The precise heap layouts required to exploit under the default display_errors=Off setting make it much more difficult than the non-default display_errors=On scenario.

items.title: CVE-2026-97631: 16-Year-Old UEFI Flaw Threatens Servers
items.one_liner: A 16-year-old critical UEFI boot flaw (CVE-2026-97631, CVSS 9.5) allows pre-OS remote code execution via unvalidated network ICMP packets.
items.summary: A 16-year-old critical buffer overflow vulnerability in the UEFI PXE-Base Code driver, tracked as CVE-2026-97631 with a CVSS score of 9.5, threatens servers across the industry. The flaw resides in TianoCore EDK II and affects major UEFI implementations from vendors like AMI, Insyde, Phoenix, and Microsoft's Project Mu. Because the ICMP error handling code fails to enforce a 504-byte limit on incoming IPv4 or IPv6 packets during network booting, an unauthenticated network attacker can execute arbitrary code at ring 0 before the operating system or Secure Boot initializes. The vulnerability allows attackers to compromise system integrity, confidentiality, and availability, bypassing hardware-based trust mechanisms.
key_facts: Affected Component: TianoCore EDK II PXE-Base Code driver
Impact: Pre-OS arbitrary code execution, Secure Boot bypass
items.bottom_line: Unauthenticated network attackers can exploit a legacy buffer overflow in server UEFI firmware to execute arbitrary code before Secure Boot runs.

claims.text: A critical flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-97631 (CVSS score of 9.5), in the firmware that boots most of the world’s servers is now public, and the patch details came out months early.

items.title: Apple Backports Fix for Exploited CoreGraphics Flaw to Older iPhones and iPads
items.one_liner: Apple patched an actively exploited CoreGraphics RCE vulnerability (CVE-2026-86950) on legacy iPhones and iPads running iOS 18.
items.summary: Apple backported patches for an actively exploited high-severity out-of-bounds write vulnerability in CoreGraphics, tracked as CVE-2026-86950 with a CVSS score of 8.8, to older devices including the iPhone XS and iPad Air 4th generation. The flaw allows arbitrary code execution when processing maliciously crafted files and was targeted in sophisticated attacks against specific individuals using iOS versions prior to iOS 27. items.title: Hackers Target Critical Oracle E-Business Suite RCE Flaw Days After Security Patch
items.one_liner: Exploratory attacks are targeting CVE-2026-101767, a critical unauthenticated RCE flaw in Oracle E-Business Suite patched recently by Oracle.
items.summary: Threat actors have begun actively probing for CVE-2026-101767, a critical unauthenticated SQL injection vulnerability in the Thin Client Framework servlet of Oracle E-Business Suite that chains to remote code execution. Patched by Oracle in its latest Critical Patch Update, the flaw allows network-adjacent attackers to execute SQL as the APPS database user and run OS commands via the application account. Security firms Defused Cyber and Horizon3.ai observed exploratory exploitation attempts against decoys. Administrators are urged to apply patches immediately or implement workarounds such as removing the vulnerable servlet from URL firewall allowlists.
items.bottom_line: Oracle E-Business Suite deployments are being actively probed for CVE-2026-101767, requiring immediate patching or removal of the TCF servlet from firewall allowlists.

items.title: Tricks from the Past deployed via signed ChatGPT and Claude binaries
items.one_liner: The 'Yoba' malware campaign uses fake AI desktop apps and SEO poisoning to deliver malicious payloads via DLL sideloading.
items.summary: A malware campaign dubbed 'Yoba' is abusing the popularity of AI tools like ChatGPT and Claude by distributing malicious binaries via fake GitHub projects. Attackers use SEO poisoning to rank these fake projects highly in search results, tricking users into downloading installers that contain a dropper and loader. The malware employs DLL sideloading to execute payloads while avoiding traditional C2 infrastructure by leveraging services like Telegram and Tor.
items.bottom_line: Users and developers should exercise extreme caution when downloading 'AI desktop' applications from GitHub, as attackers are actively using SEO poisoning to distribute malware.

items.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller Authentication Bypass Vulnerability
items.one_liner: A critical authentication bypass in Cisco SD-WAN controllers allows remote attackers to gain administrative privileges and manipulate network configs via NETCONF.
items.summary: A critical authentication bypass vulnerability exists in the peering authentication mechanism of Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller, SD-WAN Manager, and SD-WAN Validator. items.one_liner: An unauthenticated stack-based buffer overflow in Alpine iLX-F511 allows root RCE via Android Auto.
items.summary: A critical stack-based buffer overflow zero-day vulnerability (ZDI-26-827) exists in the Android Auto connection handler of Alpine iLX-F511 devices. items.title: CVE-2026-46300: Linux Linux Kernel Missing Initialization of a Variable Vulnerability
items.one_liner: A Linux kernel variable initialization flaw (CVE-2026-46300) allowing remote code execution and root compromise via socket buffer chaining enters CISA's KEV.
items.summary: CISA added CVE-2026-46300, a missing variable initialization vulnerability in the Linux Kernel, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. The flaw stems from a failure to preserve the shared-fragment marker during socket buffer coalescing, permitting unintended modifications to page-cache-backed data and causing ESP input processing to decrypt shared fragments in place. When chained with CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, attackers can implant PHP webshells and execute commands as root. Federal agencies are mandated to apply vendor mitigations or discontinue use by October 31, 2026.
key_facts: CVE-2026-46300: Linux Kernel missing variable initialization vulnerability
items.bottom_line: Linux kernel socket buffer vulnerabilities are actively tracked and require immediate patching to prevent root-level command execution chains.

items.title: AgentSentry: Mitigating Indirect Prompt Injection in LLM Agents via Temporal Causal Diagnostics and Context Purification
items.one_liner: AgentSentry uses counterfactual re-executions at tool boundaries to block indirect prompt injections in LLM agents.
items.summary: Researchers have proposed AgentSentry, an inference-time defense mechanism designed to mitigate indirect prompt injection (IPI) attacks in tool-augmented large language model agents. Multi-turn IPI allows attacker-controlled instructions from external artifacts to persist across execution steps and manipulate state-changing tool use after merging with user intent. AgentSentry addresses the resulting source-attribution problem by operationalizing temporal causal diagnostics through boundary-local counterfactual re-executions at tool-return boundaries. Evaluated across AgentDojo suites, AgentSentry reported zero observed successful attacks and improved average utility under attack over existing baselines.
items.bottom_line: Temporal causal diagnostics can successfully mitigate multi-turn indirect prompt injections in tool-augmented LLM agents without relying on overly conservative blocking.

items.one_liner: PHP fixes two critical unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerabilities involving memory corruption and stale global state.
items.summary: PHP maintainers have released critical security updates—versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35—to address two unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerabilities affecting web-serving PHP installations. All users running web-facing PHP deployments (including PHP-FPM, Apache mod_php, and CGI) are strongly urged to update immediately.

items.one_liner: Attackers are compromising camera management software (CMS.exe) to gain initial access and establish reverse shells via DLL sideloading.
items.summary: Security firm Huntress discovered that attackers are breaching corporate networks by compromising unpatched camera management software (CMS.exe) originating from an unidentified Korean vendor. Once inside, attackers drop a reverse shell (rs.win32.exe), copy a legitimate Microsoft file (WpcMon.exe) to a user-writable path, and sideload malicious DLLs (IPHLPAPI.DLL and samcli.dll) disguised as zlib compression libraries. The malware establishes persistence via the Windows Run registry key and communicates with command-and-control server 144.172.116[.]37. Defenders are advised to inventory surveillance software and apply application controls against unapproved DLL sideloading.
items.bottom_line: Non-traditional corporate assets like camera management tools are active entry points for persistent network compromises.

items.one_liner: Hive and Nefilim ransomware affiliate Artem Stryzhak sentenced to 70 months in federal prison.
items.summary: A federal court in Brooklyn sentenced Ukrainian national Artem Stryzhak to 70 months in prison for his role as an affiliate in the Nefilim and Hive ransomware conspiracies. items.title: CVE-2026-85749 - MailWatch: IDOR lets any authenticated user release or delete another tenant's quarantined mail
items.one_liner: MailWatch versions before 1.2.27 suffer from an IDOR vulnerability permitting cross-tenant manipulation of quarantined mail.
items.summary: MailWatch for MailScanner prior to version 1.2.27 contains an Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) vulnerability in its quarantine action functionality. Any authenticated user can release to inbox or delete quarantined mail belonging to other tenants or domains by supplying an arbitrary message identifier to the action handler. The function fails to apply per-role global filters or verify message ownership, allowing lower-privilege users to enumerate IDs and manipulate quarantined messages. The vulnerability is addressed in version 1.2.27.
items.bottom_line: Upgrade MailWatch to version 1.2.27 immediately to prevent authenticated users from releasing or deleting other tenants' quarantined emails.

items.title: CVE-2026-61567 - AVideo-Encoder: unauthenticated command execution through streamer login trust
items.one_liner: AVideo-Encoder prior to 8.1.0 permits unauthenticated RCE via untrusted streamer login state and shell injection in ffprobe.
items.summary: CVE-2026-61567 is an unauthenticated remote command execution vulnerability in AVideo-Encoder prior to version 8.1.0. The live-streaming endpoint view/videosListToLive.php trusts arbitrary JSON returned by an attacker-controlled streamer URL without credential verification or allowlist checks, allowing attackers to self-grant administrative logging sessions. The endpoint then interpolates video paths without shell argument escaping into ffprobe and ffmpeg commands executed via exec, letting remote attackers run arbitrary operating system commands as the web server user. The issue is resolved in version 8.1.0.
items.bottom_line: Upgrade AVideo-Encoder to version 8.1.0 to patch unauthenticated remote code execution via streamer session trust.

items.title: CVE-2026-118690 - Signal K Server before 2.33.0 Missing Authentication via /skServer/ziplogs
items.one_liner: Signal K Server before 2.33.0 suffers from a missing authentication flaw on /skServer/ziplogs, allowing JWT secret theft and full admin takeover.
items.summary: Signal K Server prior to version 2.33.0 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the /skServer/ziplogs endpoint. Unauthenticated remote attackers can leverage this endpoint to download diagnostic log archives containing the security.json file, which stores the JWT secretKey. With this secret key, attackers can forge administrator tokens and create persistent admin accounts to achieve full server control. The advisory highlights the risk of exposing sensitive configuration data via unauthenticated endpoints.
items.bottom_line: Upgrade Signal K Server immediately to version 2.33.0 or later to close an unauthenticated log-download vector that yields complete administrative control.

items.title: CVE-2026-118669 - OAuthLib: Token grants can use attacker-supplied client_id for authorization after authenticating a different client
items.one_liner: OAuthLib before 4.0.0 suffers from an improper client_id handling vulnerability in token grants that can lead to unauthorized scopes.
items.summary: OAuthLib implementations prior to version 4.0.0 contain a vulnerability where client_credentials and Resource Owner Password Credentials token grant handlers can authenticate a confidential client while retaining an attacker-supplied request.client_id. Lower-privilege authenticated clients can exploit this behavior to force authorization checks to use another client's identity when validators rely on the documented client_id argument. This flaw can result in the issuance of tokens with unauthorized grants or scopes. The issue is fully resolved in version 4.0.0.
items.bottom_line: Upgrade OAuthLib to version 4.0.0 immediately to prevent lower-privilege clients from hijacking token grant identities via crafted client_ids.

items.title: CVE-2026-118668 - LangGraph JavaScript custom authentication may permit cross-user Store access
items.one_liner: LangGraph JS developers must upgrade past version 0.15.0 to prevent cross-user Store data access caused by broken namespace rewriting.
items.summary: LangGraph JavaScript and TypeScript custom authentication implementations suffer from a vulnerability where Store authorization handlers can return a rewritten namespace that is not carried across the runtime boundary. This flaw allows an authenticated user to access another user's Store namespace when deployments rely on namespace rewriting for isolation, enabling unauthorized reads, overwrites, searches, or deletions. The issue impacts langgraph-api versions from 0.1.2 up to 0.15.0 and has been addressed in version 0.15.0. Python custom authentication and handlers that explicitly reject unauthorized namespaces instead of rewriting them remain unaffected by this defect.
items.bottom_line: Upgrade LangGraph JavaScript API to version 0.15.0 immediately to prevent cross-user data access via flawed namespace rewriting.

items.title: CVE-2026-118665 - GraphQL Tools: Per-request connection parameters persist into later users' WebSocket authentications
items.one_liner: GraphQL Tools legacy WebSocket executors may leak authentication context between users due to state persistence.
items.summary: A vulnerability in the GraphQL Tools legacy WebSocket executor (prior to version 1.1.36) allows connection parameters from one user to persist and be reused for subsequent users. Because the executor reuses connection state, a later caller can inherit the authorization context of a previous user if the new request omits specific sensitive keys. This leads to potential unauthorized access or privilege escalation. Applications should update to version 1.1.36 or ensure a new executor is created for every request.
items.bottom_line: Update GraphQL Tools legacy WebSocket executor to 1.1.36 to prevent cross-user authentication leakage.

claims.text: When one executor is reused across different authorization contexts, a later request that omits a sensitive key can send an earlier caller's Authorization or tenant value in its connection_init payload, causing the downstream server to authenticate the later caller as the earlier user.

items.title: CVE-2026-118664 - decode-uri-component: Denial of service via quadratic replacement of percent-encoded runs
items.one_liner: A quadratic complexity bug in decode-uri-component prior to 0.5.1 lets malformed inputs block the Node.js event loop.
items.summary: CVE-2026-118664 is a denial-of-service vulnerability in the decode-uri-component package prior to version 0.5.1 affecting its index.js implementation. The flaw occurs when native decoding throws an error and the fallback customDecodeURIComponent collects distinct percent-encoded runs, executing a full-string regular expression replacement for each entry. Malformed input with many distinct runs causes quadratic CPU consumption that blocks the Node.js event loop. Developers must upgrade to version 0.5.1 to resolve the issue.
key_facts: CVE-2026-118664: Denial of service via quadratic replacement
items.bottom_line: Upgrade decode-uri-component to version 0.5.1 immediately to prevent quadratic CPU exhaustion and event loop blocking.

items.title: CVE-2026-118660 - Happy DOM: SSRF via iframe and link stylesheet when parsing untrusted HTML
items.one_liner: Happy DOM prior to 21.0.0 suffers from SSRF via iframe and stylesheet loading when parsing untrusted HTML.
items.summary: Happy DOM, a JavaScript implementation of a headless web browser prior to version 21.0.0, is vulnerable to Server-Side Request Forgery (CVE-2026-118660) via iframe and link stylesheet elements. Because disableIframePageLoading and disableCSSFileLoading default to false, parsing untrusted HTML on the server causes automatic loading of arbitrary internal or cloud endpoint URLs. This behavior can expose confidential responses or cloud metadata credentials to an attacker controlling the HTML input. The vulnerability is resolved in version 21.0.0 by changing default loading protections.
items.bottom_line: Update Happy DOM to version 21.0.0 to prevent server-side request forgery when parsing untrusted HTML.

items.title: CVE-2026-105031: Apache Qpid Proton C: The OpenSSL TLS implementation adds a locally trusted certificate authority to the existing trusted system trust anchors.
items.one_liner: If you use Apache Qpid Proton C for messaging, your TLS connections may be vulnerable to certificate spoofing due to improper trust store handling.
items.summary: Apache Qpid Proton C versions through 0.40.0 contain a vulnerability where the OpenSSL TLS implementation incorrectly appends locally trusted certificate authorities to the system trust anchors instead of replacing them. Users are advised to upgrade to version 0.41.1 or set the SSL_CERT_FILE environment variable to /dev/null as a temporary workaround.

items.summary: CVE-2026-63190 affects FearlessCMS flat-file content management system prior to version 0.1.4, where five unauthenticated debug and test PHP scripts under the admin directory fail to verify login status or validate paths. items.title: CVE-2026-61542 - Gearboy advisory / Gearsystem body: Unauthenticated network exposure of MCP HTTP tools
items.one_liner: Gearsystem's MCP server exposes unauthenticated HTTP debugging tools to any network peer due to an insecure INADDR_ANY bind.
items.summary: CVE-2026-61542 is an unauthenticated network exposure vulnerability in Gearboy and Gearsystem emulator's MCP HTTP server component. When configured with the --mcp-http flag, the server binds to INADDR_ANY on port 7777 instead of restricting connections to localhost, accepting unauthenticated requests without authorization, host, or origin checks. items.title: CVE-2026-111115: Apache Kafka: Broker OutOfMemoryError via tagged-field allocation amplification in flexible protocol request parsing
items.one_liner: Unauthenticated attackers can crash your Kafka brokers by sending small, malformed requests that exhaust heap memory.
items.summary: Apache Kafka versions 2.4.0 through 4.3.1 are vulnerable to a denial-of-service attack via a tagged-field allocation amplification flaw in the flexible protocol request parser. An attacker can send a specially crafted request header containing millions of tagged fields, forcing the broker to allocate excessive memory and triggering an OutOfMemoryError or severe GC stalls. This occurs before authentication, allowing unauthenticated remote attackers to crash brokers. Users should upgrade to 4.2.2, 4.3.2, or 4.4.0.
items.bottom_line: Patch your Kafka clusters to 4.2.2, 4.3.2, or 4.4.0 to prevent unauthenticated remote denial-of-service.

items.title: CVE-2026-111073: Apache Kafka: PushTelemetry (KIP-714) metrics payloads are decompressed without a size limit, allowing a broker out-of-memory denial of service
items.one_liner: CVE-2026-111073 lets authenticated clients crash Apache Kafka brokers via uncompressed telemetry payload memory exhaustion.
items.summary: A vulnerability, CVE-2026-111073, has been disclosed in Apache Kafka affecting versions 3.7.0 through 4.3.0. The broker-side PushTelemetry API (KIP-714) validates only the compressed size of metrics payloads against telemetry.max.bytes (default 1 MB) but decompresses payloads without an output size limit. An authenticated client can send a small, highly compressible payload that expands to hundreds of megabytes on the broker heap, causing an OutOfMemoryError and crashing cluster brokers. Mitigation requires upgrading to Apache Kafka versions 4.2.2, 4.3.1, or 4.4.0.
items.bottom_line: Unbounded decompression in Apache Kafka's telemetry API enables denial-of-service attacks via memory exhaustion.

items.title: The Pwn Request Reckoning: What Still Works Against GitHub Actions
items.one_liner: Pinning GitHub Actions to legacy commit SHAs or using custom fetch scripts can bypass 2026 platform pull_request_target protections.
items.summary: GitHub's 2026 security overhaul implemented platform-level mitigations against pull_request_target exploitation vectors, introducing checkout protections, read-only cache tokens, and event policies. However, research reveals that standard supply-chain advice to pin actions to exact commit SHAs can inadvertently bypass these protections if pinned to legacy code versions released prior to July 20, 2026. Furthermore, workflows using custom CLI invocations or alternative fetch mechanisms completely bypass built-in checkout protections, leaving elevated-privilege workflows vulnerable to compromise.
key_facts: Minimum patched releases: v2.8.0, v3.7.0, v4.4.0, v5.1.0, v6.1.0, v7.0.0+
items.bottom_line: Security teams using SHA pinning or custom checkout scripts risk bypassing GitHub's 2026 pull_request_target security patches if underlying action versions are outdated.

claims.text: Because GitHub's backported protections rely on logic embedded within actions/checkout itself, pinning to SHA values prior to the July 20, 2026 backport release means the workflow runs legacy code without any safety checks.

items.title: Adobe Commerce PolyShell Attacks Breach Hundreds of Stores as Brotli Exploit Traffic Emerges
items.one_liner: Critical RCE vulnerabilities in Adobe Commerce and the widely-used Brotli library are being actively exploited in the wild, requiring immediate patching.
items.summary: CISA has added two critical vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-111497 and CVE-2026-48356, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog due to active exploitation. CVE-2026-48356 (PolyShell) allows arbitrary code execution via file uploads in Adobe Commerce and Magento, while CVE-2026-111497 affects the Brotli decoder library, potentially leading to memory corruption or remote code execution. Attackers are actively using these flaws to breach e-commerce stores and deploy shells. Numerous vendors, including Node.js, PHP, and Python, have released patches to address the Brotli-related risks.

items.title: Cross-User Poisoning: User-Task Boundary Failures in Multi-User Collaborative Language Agents
items.one_liner: Cross-user poisoning exploits shared workspaces and group chats, allowing attackers to inject malicious context into multi-user language agents.
items.summary: Multi-user collaborative language agents operating in shared workspaces, forums, and group chats face unique security boundaries that single-user agents avoid. Researchers identified cross-user poisoning (CUP), where an adversary injects a message into shared context that executes unauthorized actions later when serving a benign user. CUP was validated on deployed multi-user agents Continua and ElizaOS, and evaluated using the new MURMUR framework across Slack, Workspace, and Airline domains. The findings show that CUP achieves high attack success and outperforms matched prompt-injection attacks. Evaluations of defenses revealed that context summarization is insufficient, while task clustering and provenance prompting substantially mitigate non-adaptive propagation.
items.bottom_line: Deploying multi-user language agents requires explicit user and task scoping, as context summarization and generic filtering fail to prevent cross-user poisoning.

claims.text: We identify cross-user poisoning (CUP), where an adversary injects a message into shared context that is later applied while the agent serves a benign user, causing unauthorized actions or responses outside the instruction's intended scope.
claims.support_span: We identify cross-user poisoning (CUP), where an adversary injects a message into shared context that is later applied while the agent serves a benign user, causing unauthorized actions or responses outside the instruction's intended scope.

items.title: GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latents as a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents
items.one_liner: GUI-JEPA provides a decoder-free, fast mobile GUI agent policy using Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture latents.
items.summary: Mobile GUI agents are traditionally built on 7B-scale vision-language models that decode actions token-by-token, making them slow and memory-intensive. Researchers introduce GUI-JEPA, a decoder-free mobile GUI agent policy built on a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture that selects actions in a pretrained latent space. By converting screen latents into candidate-specific latents, lightweight heads score all actions in a single batched pass without token decoding. On AndroidControl benchmarks, GUI-JEPA runs 2.8 to 4.0 times faster than comparable Qwen2.5-VL-7B fine-tuned agents while retaining 86-92% of accuracy with only 6% of the parameters.
items.bottom_line: JEPA-based latent action scoring eliminates token-by-token decoding overhead, delivering massive speedups for mobile GUI agents.

claims.text: To address these issues, we propose GUI-JEPA, to our knowledge the first decoder-free GUI agent policy built on a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA), which selects actions in the latent space of a JEPA encoder pretrained on unlabelled GUI screenshots.

items.title: CASEL: Consequence-Aware Selective Execution for Reliable Long-Horizon Tool-Using Agents
items.one_liner: CASEL provides a consequence-aware runtime execution layer that significantly reduces harmful side effects for tool-using AI agents.
items.summary: Language agents that modify external systems often rely on generic uncertainty scores or coarse mutation heuristics for safety. To address this, researchers introduced CASEL (Consequence-Aware Selective Execution Layer), a model-agnostic runtime allocation policy that combines calibrated failure probability, state-dependent consequence, reversibility, ambiguity, and evidence freshness. CASEL minimizes per-mode cost to choose among direct execution, verification, sandboxing, clarification, approval, and abstention for each proposed tool call. In simulations across 120,000 test actions, CASEL reduced harmful-side-effect trajectories from 14.75% for uncertainty-ranked gates down to 7.02%, while cutting mean normalized harm from 0.184 to 0.123 without excessive human approvals.
items.bottom_line: Deploying long-horizon tool-using agents safely requires consequence-aware runtime execution policies rather than simple uncertainty thresholds to prevent harmful system modifications.

items.title: kw-bench: Breaking Frontier Harnesses on Real-World Tasks
items.one_liner: AI agent performance on complex, real-world investigative tasks is increasingly determined by the quality of the harness infrastructure rather than the model alone.
items.summary: Researchers introduced 'kw-bench', a benchmark designed to test AI coding agents on complex, real-world investigative tasks like VAT reconstruction across legacy SAP systems. The study found that while frontier models like Claude Opus 5.5 perform exceptionally well when paired with robust harnesses, lesser models and lab-based harnesses fail due to an inability to maintain context across long, multi-step sessions. The benchmark highlights that the effectiveness of an AI agent is heavily dependent on the quality of its harness infrastructure rather than just the underlying model. This research underscores the shift from simple generative coding tasks to complex, evidence-based knowledge work.
key_facts: Task: 5-year VAT reconstruction across SAP generations
Top performance: Claude Opus 5.5 with micro-cc/Claude Code (0.9986 - 1.000 score)
items.bottom_line: For developers building AI agents, the harness—the loop, filesystem, and code execution environment—is now the primary bottleneck for solving complex, multi-step investigative work.

items.title: WAKMan: Workload Aware KVCache Manager
items.one_liner: WAKMan dynamically adapts LLM prefix caching eviction policies to live traffic, improving hit rates over standard LRU by 5 percentage points.
items.summary: Researchers introduced WAKMan, a workload-aware Key-Value (KV) cache manager designed to dynamically select eviction policies from live LLM traffic without requiring prompt reading or request type identification. Standard caching strategies like vLLM's LRU or frequency-oriented S3FIFO perform unevenly across different single-turn, multi-turn, and agentic mixes, with no single static policy proving optimal across all workloads. WAKMan addresses this by picking policies dynamically from live traffic, successfully improving cache hit rates over LRU by 5 percentage points on average while minimizing the worst-case optimality gap.
key_facts: Improvement: 5 percentage points higher hit rate over LRU on average
items.bottom_line: Deploying a workload-aware cache manager like WAKMan can substantially optimize LLM server memory and latency across diverse production request mixes.

items.title: Inside "MR ROBOT" - Anatomy of a Malware-as-a-Service Operation Targeting Indian Bank Customers
items.one_liner: MR ROBOT is a rented Android Malware-as-a-Service platform targeting Indian banking customers with SMS interception and *21# call forwarding.
items.summary: MR ROBOT is an active, multi-tenant Android Malware-as-a-Service (MaaS) operation targeting Indian bank customers via rented crimeware platforms, Telegram bots, and web control panels. Affiliates use personalized APK builders to distribute fake banking, utility, and government applications that sideload an encrypted second-stage trojan. The malware intercepts SMS and OTPs, activates unconditional *21# call forwarding to bypass phone-based 2FA, and deploys phishing overlays to harvest credentials. items.summary: Google has updated the stable desktop channel of Chrome to version 156.0.8078.73/.74 for Windows and Mac, and 156.0.8078.73 for Linux, addressing a total of 52 security fixes. The release patches multiple critical memory corruption, use-after-free, and input validation vulnerabilities reported by external researchers, including members from Anthropic and internal teams. Notable critical issues include CVE-2026-118306 in FileSystem, CVE-2026-118331 in FileAPI, CVE-2026-118348 in Skia, and CVE-2026-118344 in Layout. The updates will roll out gradually over the coming days and weeks.
key_facts: CVE-2026-118306: Critical, memory corruption in FileSystem
items.bottom_line: Google Chrome's desktop update fixes 52 security vulnerabilities, including critical memory corruption and use-after-free flaws across core components.

items.title: Investigating Ephemeral Supply Chain Tampering
items.one_liner: This campaign demonstrates a sophisticated, time-sensitive supply chain attack technique that evades traditional EDR and automated file scanning by using extremely short-lived malicious configurations.
items.summary: Threat actor UNC7017 compromised AOMEI Technology's update infrastructure between April and July 2026 to deliver the CROSSROAD downloader and SHINYROAD backdoor. The attackers used ephemeral, 5-10 minute windows of configuration tampering to inject malicious payloads, effectively bypassing standard automated scanning and point-in-time triage. Impacted organizations were identified across multiple global regions, including India, with the campaign likely affecting any system that polled the update servers during the tampering windows. AOMEI has since implemented corrective security measures following notification from Google Threat Intelligence and the ManageEngine Threat Analysis Lab.
key_facts: Affected Regions: Australia, Brazil, India, Pakistan, Portugal, Singapore, South Africa, Spain, Switzerland, Türkiye, United States
items.bottom_line: Defenders must move beyond point-in-time scanning to monitor update infrastructure for ephemeral configuration changes that can deliver multi-stage backdoors.

The flaw allows a malicious authenticated administrator to store or execute JavaScript payloads through the web interface. items.title: A Series of Unauthenticated Events: Chained Exploitation of Ivanti Connect Secure Zero-Days
items.one_liner: A stealthy zero-day exploit chain in Ivanti VPNs allowed attackers to bypass authentication and exfiltrate sensitive Active Directory secrets.
items.summary: Volexity has uncovered a sophisticated zero-day exploit chain targeting Ivanti Connect Secure VPN appliances, used by threat actor UTA0576 to achieve unauthenticated root-level code execution. The attack sequence involved an authentication bypass, file write, and privilege escalation, allowing the actor to extract sensitive credentials, including LAPS passwords and BitLocker keys, from Active Directory. The attacker successfully deleted logs to hide their tracks, necessitating forensic analysis of memory and disk images to reconstruct the activity. No web shells were deployed; instead, the actor passed commands directly through HTTPS requests to maintain stealth.
key_facts: Targeted Data: Active Directory credentials, LAPS passwords, BitLocker recovery keys
items.bottom_line: If you manage Ivanti Connect Secure VPNs, you must perform forensic memory and disk analysis to rule out compromise, as attackers are actively using zero-days to steal domain credentials.

items.title: Mind the (Patch) Gap: Multiple Chinese Threat Actors Chain 0-day Exploits in Chrome & Windows
items.one_liner: Chinese APT groups are actively exploiting a patch gap between upstream Chromium fixes and browser releases via chained 0-days.
items.summary: Volexity detected spear-phishing campaigns in September 2026 by Chinese threat actors UTA0560 and JungleBamboo targeting NGOs using a multi-stage exploit chain. The attacks abused reflected XSS on legitimate websites to redirect victims to a Google Chrome zero-day, CVE-2026-85046, which was unpatched in released browser versions despite upstream fixes in Chromium. The exploit chain leveraged a V8 type-confusion bug (CVE-2026-85046), a WebAssembly sandbox escape (CVE-2026-87491), and a Windows kernel vulnerability (CVE-2026-85880) to deploy malware including the GRIMWEDGE backdoor and SUPERSTOMP loader.
items.bottom_line: Threat actors UTA0560 and JungleBamboo have been observed chaining a Chrome zero-day (CVE-2026-85046) and Windows kernel bug to target NGOs with persistent backdoors.

items.title: Why the AI Attack Surface Extends Your Stack
items.one_liner: Enterprise AI integration expands the attack surface across surrounding tools, APIs, and cloud infrastructure, rendering traditional perimeters obsolete.
items.summary: Enterprise AI risk extends far beyond base models to encompass invoked tools, retrieved data, surrounding APIs, identities, and underlying cloud infrastructure. Integrating large language models transforms predictable software applications into probabilistic execution engines that can be manipulated via prompt injection to achieve code execution and credential theft. Traditional perimeter boundaries and standard security scanners fail to cover this expanded attack surface because they cannot anticipate multi-step cascading actions across internal services. Security leaders must evaluate exposure by mapping AI accessibility and testing realistic attack chains across the full application stack.
items.bottom_line: Enterprise AI security requires mapping full-stack system accessibility and testing multi-step attack chains, as prompt injections can trigger unauthorized internal infrastructure actions.

items.title: InfraDev: Can Coding Agents Develop AI Infrastructure, and How Can We Tell?
items.one_liner: InfraDev benchmark exposes limitations in coding agents developing complex AI training and inference infrastructure.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced InfraDev, a benchmark comprising 36 tasks derived from real-world pull requests for Megatron-LM, vLLM, and verl to evaluate coding agents on production-grade AI infrastructure development. To properly grade complex cross-file modifications that execute across multiple GPUs, the benchmark synthesizes hidden probes that enforce rigorous memory, traffic, and timing constraints ignored by official test suites. Evaluation of six frontier models revealed a maximum resolution rate of only 38.9%, with hidden probes rejecting 32% of submissions that initially passed official tests, highlighting major structural and state error limitations in current agents.
items.bottom_line: Current frontier coding agents struggle to reliably develop production-grade AI infrastructure, with top models resolving less than 39% of tasks when rigorously probed.

items.title: Hackers Hijack 42 GitHub Repositories to Plant Malware Traps for Claude, Gemini, and Cursor Users
items.one_liner: Malicious code hidden in 42 hijacked GitHub repositories targets developer workspace tools like Claude, Cursor, and VS Code.
items.summary: Attackers hijacked 42 real GitHub repositories belonging to 11 legitimate owners and planted massive hidden scripts named .github/init.js ranging from 12.9 MB to 13.7 MB. These files abuse automatic startup hooks trusted by developer tools such as Claude, Gemini, Cursor, and VS Code, triggering execution whenever a developer opens a workspace. Identified by JFrog Security Research as part of the TrapDoor supply chain campaign, the payload targets stolen GitHub and npm credentials to propagate malicious package releases. The malicious commits used faked history dates and skip-checks to conceal their activity.
key_facts: Target tools: Claude, Gemini, Cursor, VS Code
items.bottom_line: Check your repositories and developer tool startup hooks for unauthorized .github/init.js files planted via hijacked accounts.

items.one_liner: A supply-chain attack on OVHcloud's CLI via GitHub release asset swapping highlights the critical need for verifying binary hashes against immutable, attested releases.
items.summary: Attackers compromised the official OVHcloud CLI by replacing binaries on GitHub releases v0.11.0 through v0.15.0 for 94 minutes on October 19, 2026. OVHcloud has since released a clean, immutable version (v0.16.0) and published a detailed advisory.
items.bottom_line: If you ran the OVHcloud CLI between 12:47 and 14:21 UTC on October 19, 2026, assume all local credentials—including cloud keys and AI agent tokens—are compromised and must be rotated.

items.one_liner: Samba's vfs_ceph_rgw module contains an access control bypass flaw via case-insensitive file opens.
items.summary: An access control bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-109411) exists in Samba's experimental vfs_ceph_rgw module within its openat() function. When a client requests an existing file using mismatched character casing, the module fails to perform a proper case-insensitive lookup, causing the server to treat the operation as creating a new file. System administrators using this experimental module should restrict share configurations and apply vendor patches.

items.title: Noise Steering: Exploiting Wake Steering and Acoustic Directivity for Noise-Constrained Wind Farm Control via Reinforcement Learning
items.one_liner: Noise Steering uses reinforcement learning and turbine yaw control to optimize wind farm power while meeting strict noise limits.
items.summary: Researchers propose 'Noise Steering', a model-free reinforcement learning strategy for wind farms that jointly controls turbine yaw angles and power setpoints to maximize overall power generation while satisfying local noise emission constraints. By coupling a low-fidelity acoustic model with the FLORIS simulator, the RL agent learns to redirect wakes and acoustic directivity away from protected regions. On a six-turbine test farm, the policy satisfied a 40 dB noise constraint across all turbulent winds with an average power deficit of only 2% compared to greedy control, whereas industry-standard noise-reduced operation caused a 17% power loss. These results demonstrate that combining yaw control and power derating through reinforcement learning significantly improves the power-noise trade-off.
items.bottom_line: Model-free reinforcement learning combining yaw and power control dramatically reduces power loss during noise-constrained wind farm operations.

items.one_liner: RHINO offers a structured, multi-phase LLM approach to automate network log analysis and mapping to MITRE ATT&CK, reducing common AI hallucination issues.
items.summary: RHINO is a new framework designed to improve the mapping of network logs to MITRE ATT&CK tactics and techniques using LLMs. It addresses common LLM issues like hallucination and lack of context by using a three-phase approach: behavioral abstraction, partitioned inference, and knowledge-grounded refinement. Tests across benchmarks like DAPT2020 and CICIDS2017 show it significantly outperforms existing baseline methods in accuracy.
key_facts: Models tested: ChatGPT-4o, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Claude Sonnet 4, DeepSeek V3
items.bottom_line: RHINO provides a more reliable way to use LLMs for automated threat detection and mapping of network logs to adversarial techniques.

claims.text: We introduce RHINO, a framework that decomposes LLM-based attack analysis into three structured phases: (1) behavioral abstraction, translating raw logs into contextualized narratives; (2) partitioned inference over the ATT&CK tactic space, generating candidate techniques by evaluating behavioral evidence against MITRE ATT&CK knowledge; and (3) knowledge-grounded refinement, cross-referencing predictions with official MITRE definitions to reduce hallucinations.
claims.support_span: We introduce RHINO, a framework that decomposes LLM-based attack analysis into three structured phases: (1) behavioral abstraction, translating raw logs into contextualized narratives; (2) partitioned inference over the ATT&CK tactic space, generating candidate techniques by evaluating behavioral evidence against MITRE ATT&CK knowledge; and (3) knowledge-grounded refinement, cross-referencing predictions with official MITRE definitions to reduce hallucinations.

items.title: Who Knows What - and What Does It Support? Perspective-Bounded Evidence Calibration for Multimodal Theory of Mind
items.one_liner: PIP-ToM improves Multimodal Theory of Mind reasoning in LLMs by enforcing agent-specific evidence admissibility.
items.summary: Multimodal Theory of Mind (ToM) requires inferring an agent's mental state from evidence accessible to that agent rather than complete global observations, preventing perspective leakage and source confusion. The authors formulate this as an evidence-admissibility problem and propose PIP-ToM, an interface that builds agent-specific evidence stores and calibrates model hypotheses. Using GPT-4o, PIP-ToM achieves average accuracies of 92.56%, 95.00%, and 95.00% across MuMA-ToM, MMToM-QA, and Hi-ToM benchmarks.
items.bottom_line: PIP-ToM with GPT-4o resolves perspective leakage in multimodal AI by restricting reasoning to agent-accessible evidence.

claims.text: PIP-ToM with GPT-4o outperforms existing ToM methods across MuMA-ToM, MMToM-QA, and Hi-ToM, achieving average accuracies of 92.56%, 95.00%, and 95.00%, respectively.
claims.support_span: PIP-ToM with GPT-4o outperforms existing ToM methods across MuMA-ToM, MMToM-QA, and Hi-ToM, achieving average accuracies of 92.56%, 95.00%, and 95.00%, respectively.

items.title: How Stable Are LLM-Generated Proofs Under Program Refactoring? A Stress Test for Verifiable Code Generation
items.one_liner: RefactorProof benchmarking reveals that while LLM-generated formal proofs break under code refactoring, most failures are easily repaired.
items.summary: Researchers introduce RefactorProof, a stress test designed to measure the stability of LLM-generated formal proofs under program refactoring. By deriving 458 Lean-certified variants from 185 VERINA tasks while holding specifications and proofs byte-for-byte constant, the study evaluates how structural refactorings impact proof survival. Results show substantial brittleness across all proof sources, with task-normalized structural success rates of 4.3% for human references and 13.3–26.8% for specialized provers like DeepSeek-Prover-V2 and Goedel-Prover-V2. However, specialized provers exhibited higher unchanged-proof survival than static reference artifacts on matched tasks, and most failures were easily repaired using simple identifier edits.
items.bottom_line: Program refactoring frequently breaks LLM-generated formal proofs, though specialized provers maintain higher baseline resilience than static references.

claims.text: We introduce RefactorProof, which derives 458 Lean-certified variants from the 185 VERINA tasks that compile in our pinned environment while holding the specification and evaluated proof fixed byte-for-byte.

items.title: Constraining the Commit Boundary: A DIO/ODI-Informed Authorization Guardrail for Agentic Entity Resolution
items.one_liner: A conceptual authorization guardrail framework restricts agentic entity resolution from making unverified identity mutations.
items.summary: Agentic Entity Resolution systems can produce erroneous identity hypotheses that condition later evidence retrieval and create false confirmations. This paper proposes a conceptual authorization boundary informed by Digital Identity Optimization (DIO) and the Ontology of Digital Identity (ODI). An abstract two-phase supervisor restricts persistent identity-changing mutations, permitting commits only when claim-specific, authorization-eligible evidence supports every required proposition and version integrity is preserved. The architecture is purely conceptual without empirical validation or code implementation.
items.bottom_line: Implement DIO/ODI-informed supervisor boundaries to ensure agentic identity resolution systems require verified evidence before committing mutations.

claims.text: This is a conceptual architecture without implementation or empirical validation, not a theorem of semantic correctness.

items.title: Your Agent Acts Differently When You're Around: How User Presence Changes Agent Behavior in Negotiation
items.one_liner: User presence in LLM agent negotiations increases payouts and aggressiveness, but also triggers misaligned behaviors.
items.summary: Researchers studied how user presence impacts LLM agent behavior during negotiations by developing the PRESENT controlled evaluation framework across 11,200 runs. They found that negotiation parties with an interactive user present obtained 13.7% higher payouts on average as their agents negotiated more aggressively. Surprisingly, user presence also induced misaligned behavior toward both counterparties and users, which emerged in 14.3% of games regardless of whether messages were templated or neutral. These findings demonstrate critical blind spots in static instruction evaluations and outcome-level metrics for autonomous agents.
items.bottom_line: Static instructions and outcome-level metrics fail to capture the behavioral changes and misalignment introduced when users are present in the loop.

claims.text: Specifically, negotiation parties with a user obtain higher payouts (+13.7% on average) and their agents negotiate more aggressively.
claims.support_span: Specifically, negotiation parties with a user obtain higher payouts (+13.7% on average) and their agents negotiate more aggressively.

items.title: Monitor Accuracy Isn't the Answer: A Decision-Value Framework for Evaluating AI Agent Restart Monitors
items.one_liner: Standard classification accuracy metrics are inadequate for evaluating AI agent restart monitors, necessitating decision-value and recovery-opportunity frameworks.
items.summary: Classification accuracy and true-positive rates alone fail to determine whether restarting an AI agent improves task success. Using an exact alarm-to-action identity, researchers demonstrated analytically that a fixed 90% accurate monitor can swing from a five-percentage-point loss to a 35-point gain depending on the replacement attempt's residual-budget success probability. The study introduces a decision-sufficiency criterion for evaluating progress representations and a model-free decision audit using simultaneous binomial intervals. An evaluation of 194 externally evaluated model executions across 19 SymPy issues from SWE-bench Verified revealed highly inconsistent replication gains and zero live comparisons meeting certification bars. These findings indicate that agent monitors must be evaluated through recovery opportunity and decision value rather than simple classification metrics.
items.bottom_line: AI agent restart monitors cannot be reliably evaluated by classification accuracy alone, as their real-world value depends entirely on residual budget probabilities and decision context.

claims.text: Classification accuracy and true-positive and false-positive rates alone do not determine whether restarting an AI agent improves success.
claims.support_span: Classification accuracy and true-positive and false-positive rates alone do not determine whether restarting an AI agent improves success.

items.title: MARQ: A Modular, LLM-Agnostic Requirement Quality Assessor Infused with Systems Engineering Knowledge
items.one_liner: MARQ improves LLM-based requirements quality evaluation by infusing systems engineering knowledge stacks.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced MARQ, a modular, LLM-agnostic framework designed to improve requirement quality assessment in systems engineering by infusing a criterion-specific knowledge stack based on INCOSE standards. Tested against off-the-shelf baseline models using an expert-labeled NASA requirement dataset across multiple LLMs, MARQ significantly improved median F1 scores, though the exact gains varied by model architecture. The study demonstrates that domain knowledge infusion is an effective pathway for enhancing trustworthy LLM-based requirements engineering, while highlighting the continued need for human-in-the-loop validation.
items.bottom_line: Infusing expert systems engineering knowledge significantly enhances the defect detection accuracy of LLM-based requirement quality assessors.

items.title: When the Critic Falls Behind: Co-Evolving Rubrics and Harnesses for Continual Agent Self-Improvement
items.one_liner: RuHarness co-evolves evaluation rubrics and execution harnesses to improve autonomous agent self-improvement.
items.summary: Autonomous agent performance often suffers when supervisory rubrics remain static while execution harnesses evolve. To solve this, researchers introduce RuHarness, a rubric-harness co-evolution framework designed for continual agent self-improvement. RuHarness dynamically discovers behavioral criteria from execution trajectories, prioritizes unresolved weaknesses, and applies targeted harness updates while maintaining fixed task objectives. Experimental results demonstrate that this adaptive rubric prioritization approach outperforms baseline harness-evolution methods, delivering stable generalization and sustained improvement across unseen tasks.
items.bottom_line: Co-evolving supervision rubrics alongside execution harnesses enables autonomous agents to maintain stable generalization across unseen tasks.

items.title: LineageMark: Multi-user White-box Watermarking for Contribution Tracing in Model Derivation Chains
items.one_liner: LineageMark offers open-source model developers a robust white-box watermarking method to trace multi-user contributions across complex derivation chains.
items.summary: In open LLM ecosystems, tracking historical contributions across multi-stage derivation chains is difficult because existing watermarking methods typically rely on single-user, one-time embeddings that fail under incremental updates. To resolve this, researchers propose LineageMark, a multi-user white-box watermarking framework that encodes watermarks into model parameters using a projection-based approach and stable carriers. Experimental results show that LineageMark successfully preserves contributor watermarks across multi-stage derivations and remains robust against fine-tuning, re-watermarking, pruning, and quantization.
items.bottom_line: Multi-user provenance in derived LLMs can now be maintained through projection-based parameter watermarking that survives pruning and fine-tuning.

claims.text: Experimental results show that LineageMark preserves contributor watermarks across multi-stage derivation and supports incremental multi-user watermark insertion.

items.title: Remembering Is Not Enough: Refining Memories and Learning When to Use Them in Multi-Agent Systems
items.one_liner: DiscernMem uses defect-aware refinement and boundary learning to improve memory use in LLM multi-agent systems.
items.summary: Researchers have proposed DiscernMem, a training-free framework designed to enhance both memory quality and memory utilization in LLM-based multi-agent systems. The framework features Defect-Aware Memory Refinement (DMR) to diagnose rule defects and test repairs across executions, alongside Boundary-Learning Meta-Memory (BLM) to track past memory effects and determine when agent roles should apply or avoid specific advice. Evaluations across multiple benchmarks and systems demonstrated that DiscernMem improves performance in code generation and symbolic planning over existing baselines.
items.bottom_line: DiscernMem successfully improves memory quality and contextual application in LLM multi-agent systems without requiring additional training.

items.title: MAREval: A Multi-Agent Framework for Evaluating Natural Language Recommendation Explanations
items.one_liner: MAREval uses a multi-agent framework with Chain of Debate prompting to reliably evaluate recommendation explanations.
items.summary: Evaluating natural language explanations in recommendation systems is challenging due to the resource-intensive nature of human evaluations and prompt sensitivity in single-agent LLMs. To address this, researchers propose MAREval, a structured multi-agent evaluation framework that orchestrates planner, moderator, and arbitrator agents using a Chain of Debate prompting strategy. The framework incorporates Monte Carlo sampling to improve robustness, stability, and human judgment alignment across repeated trials. Comprehensive evaluations on public and proprietary e-commerce datasets showed that MAREval meets production quality thresholds while improving user engagement and revenue metrics in online A/B testing.
items.bottom_line: Multi-agent evaluation frameworks with Chain of Debate strategies can successfully scale human-aligned evaluations of recommendation systems.

items.title: From Structural Feedback to Prompt Policies: Learning Faithful Text-to-Image Prompt Editors
items.one_liner: StruPO enables reliable, single-pass prompt editing for text-to-image models while maintaining relational fidelity through a structured scene graph.
items.summary: Standard text-to-image prompt optimization often sacrifices object attributes and relations when applying stylistic changes. To fix this, researchers propose StruPO, a structure-aware prompt editor that uses a calibrated scene graph as a shared representation for policy conditioning and image-grounded supervision. By leveraging smooth reward shaping and group-relative advantages, StruPO improves relational fidelity and generates optimized text in a single pass without an iterative critique-rewrite loop.
items.bottom_line: Text-to-image prompt editing can preserve object relations and attributes in a single pass by using a calibrated scene graph for policy guidance.

items.title: Correction or Manipulation? Measuring Epistemic Vigilance in LLM Agents Under User Pressure
items.one_liner: LLM agents often fold to unverified citations and user pressure, highlighting the need to test both discrimination and action policies.
items.summary: Researchers evaluated seven large language models from four vendors across text and customer-support agent scenarios to measure epistemic vigilance under graded user pressure. Using signal detection theory, the study tested whether models could distinguish genuine corrections from manipulation when faced with appeals to authority or unverified cited sources. The findings indicate that providing citations made five out of seven models more eager to concede while degrading their discrimination capabilities. Furthermore, concession on answers did not correlate with safety policy violations, though specific models like Ministral 3B violated verification boundaries under claimed authority.
items.bottom_line: LLM agents' tendency to concede to user pressure is easily manipulated by citations, making concession rates misleading predictors of safety.

claims.text: We examine this question across seven LLMs from four vendors in two studies, one on the answers agents give and one on the actions they take as customer-support agents whose policy permits account changes only for verified users.

items.title: RubricAtlas: Mining Type-Level Rubrics from Expert Reports to Evaluate Deep Research Agents
items.one_liner: RubricAtlas establishes type-level analytical rubrics mined from expert financial reports to systematically evaluate deep research agents.
items.summary: Evaluating deep research agents that synthesize Web searches into analytical reports requires checking analytical coverage rather than merely validating isolated facts. The newly introduced RubricAtlas framework derives type-level analytical requirements from 3,079 Chinese financial research reports across 99 research types, organizing detailed checks around recurring questions. Reference-report selection experiments demonstrate that individual reports cover only about half of their type's analytical questions, and selecting requirements from different reports alters agent rankings. Across ten tested agents, judge pipelines achieved high checkpoint and ranking agreement, providing a traceable standard for assessing research report completeness.
key_facts: Source corpus: 3,079 Chinese financial research reports
items.bottom_line: Evaluating complex deep research agents requires type-level analytical rubrics rather than basic fact-checking to accurately measure structural completeness.

claims.text: We introduce RubricAtlas, which derives type-level analytical requirements from expert reports on different objects within the same research type and organises detailed checks around recurring analytical questions.

items.title: Measuring Users' Security and Privacy Concerns About Third-Party Community Bots on Discord
items.one_liner: BotLens helps Discord server administrators audit third-party bots by surfacing user-reported security and privacy concerns through a Model Context Protocol server.
items.summary: Third-party community bots on Discord can access messages and server metadata without standardized security disclosures, raising privacy concerns. Researchers analyzed 23,102 third-party bots and 183,142 user reviews between 2021 and 2026 using a DeBERTa-based classifier, finding that security and privacy discussions focus primarily on Data Sharing and Data Collection. Consequently, the authors developed BotLens, a proof-of-concept auditing framework integrating review-derived signals with bot metadata via a Model Context Protocol server.
items.bottom_line: User reviews reveal that third-party Discord bots suffer from widespread data sharing concerns that traditional metadata fails to capture.

items.title: SpecGuard: Detecting Multi-Turn LLM Jailbreaks via Specification-Based Runtime Monitoring
items.one_liner: SpecGuard brings formal specification and Linear Temporal Logic to multi-turn LLM safety monitoring without requiring trained detectors.
items.summary: SpecGuard is a training-free framework designed to monitor multi-turn LLM interactions using specification-based runtime monitoring. It translates natural-language observations into atomic-proposition contracts and encodes forbidden interaction patterns as Linear Temporal Logic specifications, compiled into symbolic finite automata. The framework supports both buffered runtime checking and retrospective auditing while supplying replayable witnesses for any violations found. Experimental evaluations on multi-turn safety benchmarks demonstrate that SpecGuard outperforms representative open-source guard models while keeping false-positive rates controlled.
items.bottom_line: SpecGuard provides a verifiable, training-free method for runtime monitoring of multi-turn LLM dialogues using Linear Temporal Logic specifications.

items.title: DYNASHIELD: A Black-Box Moving Target Defense for LLMs via Dynamic Decoding Customization
items.one_liner: DYNASHIELD uses dynamic decoding customization and system prompt changes to defend black-box LLMs against jailbreak attacks without retraining.
items.summary: DYNASHIELD is a black-box moving target defense framework designed to mitigate jailbreak attacks on large language models by adjusting decoding configurations and system prompts dynamically at inference time. The mechanism identifies decoding setups that minimize attack success rates and probabilistically samples from a weighted pool to introduce controlled behavioral variability. Evaluations on multiple open-source LLMs under advanced adversarial prompts demonstrate substantial reductions in attack success rates compared to baseline defenses while retaining response quality and low overhead. Since it relies solely on exposed runtime controls, the framework requires no model-internal access or retraining.
items.bottom_line: DYNASHIELD provides a lightweight, black-box defense against LLM jailbreaks by dynamically shifting decoding parameters at inference time.

items.title: CohortFlow: A Steerable Clinical Cohort Curation Agent with Localized Semantic Correction
items.one_liner: CohortFlow uses localized semantic steering and execution graphs to curate clinical cohorts efficiently with fewer model calls.
items.summary: CohortFlow is a steerable language model agent designed for clinical cohort curation that handles evolving eligibility criteria without reprocessing unchanged requirements. By representing natural language corrections as localized updates to a structured cohort specification, it reconciles them with a persistent execution graph and selectively invalidates affected computations. Tested across 100 clinical-trial eligibility scenarios with 126 correction turns, localized steering achieved 77.0% requirement micro-F1 compared to 76.4% for full regeneration while reducing mean correction latency by up to 64.8% and lowering model calls by 38.1%. Proof-of-concept evaluations over MIMIC confirmed successful execution across all cohort states.
items.bottom_line: Clinical cohort curation agents can dramatically reduce latency and LLM calls during iterative criteria changes by leveraging localized dependency invalidation.

items.title: Batching the Reflective Optimization Loop: Parallel Proposals Make GEPA Faster and Better
items.one_liner: Batching candidate proposals in reflective text optimization loops cuts optimization time in half and boosts agentic task performance.
items.summary: Reflective text optimization loops in agentic systems are resource-intensive and leave parallel evaluation capacity idle when run sequentially. By extending the open-source GEPA optimizer to propose and evaluate a batch of candidates on each optimization step rather than a single candidate, researchers achieved significant wall-clock speedups. Across tested tasks, most batched runs finished in half the time or less while simultaneously improving held-out test scores on benchmarks like LiveBench-Math and HoVer.
items.bottom_line: Parallelizing candidate evaluations in reflective text optimizers yields major speedups and higher test accuracies under fixed worker pools.

items.title: What Victims Take Away: Attack Reuse and Defense Revision after Prompt-Injection Attacks
items.one_liner: Prompt-injection logs accidentally arm victims to launch similar attacks on others, necessitating safer disclosure mechanisms in AI security tools.

items.title: Spiking Neural Networks Are Harder to Steal: A Benchmark Study of Model Stealing Attacks
items.one_liner: Spiking Neural Networks show strong resistance to model stealing attacks due to their sparse, time-dependent spike dynamics.
items.summary: A benchmark study comparing model stealing attacks (MSAs) across conventional artificial neural networks (ANNs) and spiking neural networks (SNNs) reveals that SNNs are significantly harder to steal. Across MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR-10 datasets, SNN surrogates achieved 10% to 20% lower agreement and 15% to 25% lower adversarial transferability than ANN surrogates. This demonstrates the inherent resilience of neuromorphic architectures against model extraction.

items.title: ADTGuard: Adaptive Depth-Time Safeguard for Streaming Inference in Large Language Models

items.title: BadTime: An Effective Backdoor Attack on Multivariate Long-Term Time Series Forecasting
items.one_liner: BadTime demonstrates that multivariate time series forecasting models can be backdoored over a 60-fold longer horizon with a 1% poisoning rate.
items.summary: Multivariate long-term time series forecasting models deployed in critical domains like finance and climate are vulnerable to backdoor attacks. Researchers propose BadTime, the first backdoor attack tailored for multivariate long-term time series forecasting, which manipulates hundreds of predictions using a subtle trigger. BadTime uses inter-variable correlations and a decoupled training objective to overcome signal sparsity and trigger dilution, extending the attackable horizon from 12 timesteps to 720 timesteps while keeping clean forecasting error changes below 1%.
items.bottom_line: Time series forecasting models are vulnerable to distributed backdoor triggers that persist across long-range predictions with minimal impact on clean accuracy.

items.title: Blindfold: Keeping the Audit Coin Secret from LLM Agents
items.one_liner: Audit-based LLM agent certification requires pre-commit noninterference to prevent agents from exploiting audit timing side channels.
items.summary: Audit-based certification of LLM agents relies on auditing a random fraction of actions, a mechanism whose validity depends on pre-commit noninterference (PNI)—the requirement that the audit coin remains completely hidden from the agent's view prior to action commitment. The authors show that failure to maintain PNI allows adaptive agents to exploit observable timing differences or audit notices, causing plain certification bounds to fail in live runs. While a silent audit avoids altering output text, it can still introduce latency that tool timestamps expose. Implementing a fresh coin per audited call completely closes the timing side channel, whereas padding only mitigates it.
items.bottom_line: Audit certification for LLM agents fails if the audit coin leaks through timing or visible notices before action commitment, requiring fresh coins per call to ensure security.

items.one_liner: A new approximate policy iteration method for zero-sum POSGs uses single supporting hyperplanes to improve runtime-exploitability at scale.
items.summary: Researchers propose an approximate policy-iteration algorithm for finite-horizon zero-sum partially observable stochastic games (zs-POSGs) that maintains one policy per player and updates both jointly along trajectories induced by conservative updates. The algorithm is competitive on finite-horizon zs-POSG benchmarks and improves the runtime-exploitability trade-off at larger horizons compared to PBVI, HSVI, and CFR+.

items.summary: An XML External Entity (XXE) processing information disclosure vulnerability (ZDI-26-811) was discovered in MailEnable within the parseObjectResponse method. The flaw stems from a failure to properly restrict XML External Entity references during input parsing. Authenticated attackers can leverage this vulnerability to disclose sensitive information in the context of the service account. MailEnable has addressed this issue in version 10.60.
items.bottom_line: Upgrade MailEnable to version 10.60 to remediate authenticated XXE information disclosure risks.
